page: UpCloud PREMIUM-80xCPU-512GB is a KVM-based virtual server powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 80 vCPUs mapped to 80 physical cores with a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz and a shared CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing 6.4 GB of memory per core, and includes a bundled 500 GB local SSD storage volume alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core CPU capabilities, with the stress-ng multi-core test and PassMark CPU score both placing in the top 10%. Cryptographic and compression workloads perform exceptionally well, as evidenced by top-tier results in PassMark CPU encryption and single-threaded gzip compression. Memory performance is mixed; while cached small-block read bandwidth reaches a top-tier 9301.72 GB/sec, the PassMark memory score is average. Redis SET operations demonstrate outstanding throughput at 124.66 million operations per second.

Despite the high core count and strong computational throughput, this server exhibits weak performance in LLM text generation, making it less suitable for real-time AI inference workloads. The shared CPU allocation model represents a potential resource-sharing tradeoff, though the high density of 80 physical cores and 512 GB RAM offers high resource capacity. This hardware profile is highly cost-efficient for parallel processing tasks, large-scale database operations, static web serving, and heavy decompression workloads.
